Harmonize BDHS variables across survey rounds

Source: R/harmonize.R
bdhs_harmonize.Rd

Creates analysis-ready variables that mean the same thing in every BDHS round, from 1993-94 to 2022. DHS codes change between rounds (new divisions, re-ordered region codes, new answer categories, letters of the delivery-assistance variables, ...) and some value labels in the files are wrong; the bundled crosswalk records, for every round, which source variables and codes to use. See bdhs_harmonized_vars() for the catalogue.

Usage

bdhs_harmonize(
  data,
  vars = NULL,
  survey = NULL,
  recode = NULL,
  prefix = "",
  warn = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame of BDHS recode data with the original DHS codes (haven-labelled or plain numeric), as returned by bdhs_read(), bdhs_simulate() or bdhs_pool().

vars

Names of harmonized variables to create (see bdhs_harmonized_vars()). NULL (default) creates every variable that applies to the recode.

survey

Optional survey reference for data from a single round, overriding detection.

recode

Optional recode code ("KR", "IR", ...), overriding detection.

prefix

A prefix for the new column names, e.g. "h_".

warn

If TRUE (default), warn about unexpected codes and label drift.

Value

data with the harmonized columns added (or replaced) and its attributes kept. The attribute bdhs_harmonized lists the harmonized columns.

Details

The data can come from one round (detected from the bdhs_survey_id attribute or v000/v007) or from several rounds stacked with bdhs_pool() (a survey_id column), in which case every row is harmonized with the rules of its own round.

  • Factors get the documented levels (in documented order); binary variables are integer 0/1; numeric variables are on their natural scale (z-scores divided by 100, weights by 1e6, ...).

  • Variables whose source variables are absent from data are skipped (one message lists them).

  • Rounds where a variable was not collected, or where it lives in a separate WI (wealth index) or HW (WHO height/weight) file, give NA with a message. Merge those files first with bdhs_merge() and the variable is computed from them.

  • Codes not covered by the rules become NA with a warning, and value labels that no longer match the expected meaning (label drift, e.g. data attributed to the wrong round) are reported, unless warn = FALSE. Codes whose labels mark them as missing / don't know / not de jure are set to NA silently.

Rules are written for the children's recode (KR); woman-level rules also apply to the women's (IR) and births (BR) recodes, and variables with a household equivalent (household_var in bdhs_harmonized_vars()) to the household (HR) and household member (PR) recodes.

Examples

kr <- bdhs_simulate(2014, "KR")
h <- bdhs_harmonize(kr, vars = c("division_trend6", "residence", "child_age_months"))
table(h$division_trend6)
#> 
#>   barishal chattogram      dhaka     khulna   rajshahi     sylhet 
#>         51         56         57         31         64         27 

# Pooled rounds are harmonized round by round
pooled <- bdhs_pool(bdhs_simulate(2011, "IR"), bdhs_simulate(2022, "IR"))
#> ℹ Value labels differ between rounds for 3 columns; kept the codes and dropped
#>   the labels: `v022`, `v023`, and `v024`.
#> ℹ DHS codes are not always comparable across rounds; use `harmonize = TRUE` or
#>   `bdhs_harmonize()` for comparable variables.
h <- bdhs_harmonize(pooled, vars = c("division_surveyed", "division_trend6"))
table(h$survey_id, h$division_trend6)
#>            
#>             barishal chattogram dhaka khulna rajshahi sylhet
#>   BD2011DHS      108        114   113     54      109     53
#>   BD2022DHS      112        113   111     54      107     55
